how: Members recruit named users and ask for help with a border, adjacent fill and defense.
A tagged member answers the summons with a bare acceptance.
The direct summons receives a bare acceptance, establishing one local call-and-answer pair.
An offer asking how to help elicits concrete placement instructions rather than ending with a bare acceptance.
Members negotiate border colour and elaborate a hotstopper design in adjacent space.
Design accommodation can retain a contrary preference when participants prioritise defending the flag.
Members report a completed corner and continued survival of the flag.
A helper receives an anchor location and a pixel-placement instruction.
The visible design compromise and later coordinate instruction do not show a template settling the border dispute.
Attempting defensive automation can end in repeated technical errors without demonstrating added placements.
The failed defensive script report supplies no comparison between manual capacity and the work required.
Voluntary design accommodation supports informal local coordination but cannot establish whether organisational rules existed elsewhere or test the cross-room prevalence claim.
The first display already shows the mark standing, leaving its original starter unidentified.
Members report recapture, urge vigilance and try to recreate a flag that is no longer there.
A member tries to attribute rapid overwriting to Blue and tentatively associates that colour with a named person.
Attribution remains provisional when its supporting report explicitly uses uncertainty rather than identifying a verified placer.
Upkeep cannot be treated as following completion exclusively because recapture and vigilance already appear before the completed-corner report.
Judging one adjacent patch too small for useful art does not establish that the room lacks capacity for its flag.
Disagreement over a flag border concerns colour rather than a negotiated territorial agreement.
Internal design accommodation and reconstruction in claimed space do not demonstrate restraint toward another room.
An individual offer and placement instruction do not establish help exchanged between rooms.
The individual help exchange does not establish a coalition.
The design objection concerns colour preference rather than authority to bind a room to an external agreement.
Without an evidenced inter-room agreement, the colour disagreement cannot test an agreement-to-authority-dispute mechanism.
A display above the podcast logo does not establish hosting rules or permission.
The direct help exchange provides placement guidance without an envoy carrying a proposal to another room.
Reconstruction coordinates do not establish relocation, while the explicit successor invitation invokes closure rather than defeat at an old spot.
Participants joke through podcast references, changing monsters to heroes and crediting Odin with stopping a script.
The visible podcast jokes instantiate enacted lore without establishing that the same jokes or quarrel predated the canvas.
A suspected Blue attack and an unspecified offensive do not establish a pre-canvas quarrel.
Tentative attribution and an offensive without a named target cannot establish an inherited tie naming an attacked rival.
Canvas jokes about heroes and Odin do not demonstrate a separate host-sub April Fools prank.
Visible recruitment and defense calls do not establish moderation or a boundary around canvas talk.
Calls alone do not establish a canvas-post flood or a host response to that flood.
Members display the flag, thank helpers and celebrate provisional survival and doubling.
Members mourn former glory and report a mixed ending in which the flag stands but the podcast logo is lost.
Celebration and later fate reporting support descriptive order without establishing that celebration prompted preservation.
A member invokes the original canvas ending and invites builders to continue on a replacement.
Continuation on a successor canvas renews the call for builders rather than only retaining an image.
A later continuation invitation cites closure without establishing that an earlier ending report caused the move.
An ending report, a podcast joke and a successor invitation do not establish contention over which historical canvas version should be kept.
An unspecified offensive call supports offensive intent without identifying its target, intended alteration or execution.
A feared attack and an internal status joke do not establish a contest conducted in talk with an identified rival room.
The offensive thread visibly elicits mourning and offers of help rather than a refusal or apology.
